E1.evidence: Dockerfile-based reproducer (ros:humble, rmw_cyclonedds_cpp with CYCLONEDDS_URI SharedMemory enabled, iox-roudi, `ros2 topic pub /clock ... -r 10000`, repeated `ros2 run rclcpp_components component_container --ros-args -p use_sim_time:=true`), the crash text "what():  cannot store a negative time point in rclcpp::Time", a Valgrind use-after-free trace, and maintainer agreement ("once the memory is returned to the underlying middleware, they should be considered invalid").

E2.evidence: With shared memory enabled, rmw_cyclonedds_cpp marks the subscription loan-capable ("rmw_subscription->can_loan_messages = sub->is_loaning_available;") and hands out a loaned sample that it frees when the loan is returned (comment: "will be released when `rmw_return_loaned_message_from_subscription()` is called"; Valgrind: freed by dds_data_allocator_free in rmw_return_loaned_message_from_subscription). rclcpp wraps the loan in a non-owning shared_ptr (subscription.hpp: "// message is loaned, so we have to make sure that the deleter does not deallocate the message"), its TimeSource caches that pointer ("last_msg_set_ = msg;"), and its executor returns the loan right after the callback; a later read of the cached clock message reads memory rmw_cyclonedds_cpp has already freed. The defect is the timing of the loan return relative to rclcpp's use of provider-owned memory, i.e. it depends on the loan-lifetime agreement across the rclcpp/RMW boundary and does not occur when the peer does not loan (reporter: only with Iceoryx enabled; maintainer: "if you use the non-loaned APIs, it works exactly as you expect"). Not wiring or build.

E3.evidence: PAIR: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp's loaned /clock sample (output) is consumed by rclcpp's subscription/TimeSource; the crash is observed during node startup while the two run together.

E4.evidence: Observed: "Random nodes fail startup with the following exception:" followed by "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'", plus a Valgrind "Invalid read of size 8" whose block was "free'd" in rmw_return_loaned_message_from_subscription.

units.name: rclcpp
units.revision_basis: The reporter uses the official ros:humble Docker image (digest sha256:12cc6355..., report 2023-09-18) with apt binaries; the digest's manifest could not be retrieved from the registry (MANIFEST_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED). The latest rclcpp Humble release before the report is 16.0.5 (52327dd3, 2023-07-17); 16.0.6 was tagged 2023-09-19, after the report; if the image predates the July 2023 Humble sync it would carry 16.0.4, but time_source.cpp, executor.cpp and subscription.hpp are unchanged between 16.0.4 and 16.0.5. The reporter's links point at humble head 724b4588 (2023-09-16) for reading the code, not as the installed version. Resolved: 16.0.7 (47712ecf, 2023-11-13), the Humble release containing backport #2364 (24f059c5), released together with rcl 5.3.6.

units.name: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
units.revision_basis: Installed by `apt-get install -y ros-$ROS_DISTRO-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp` in the ros:humble image in September 2023; tag 1.3.4 (7cb3b38a, 2022-11-07) is the last Humble release and the humble branch has no commits between 2022-11-08 and 2023-11-30. The resolution does not change this unit.

failed_conditions.quote: That said, I see exactly what you mean about the loaned APIs.  They do not work like that; once the memory is returned to the underlying middleware, they should be considered invalid.

loudness_evidence: No tooling diagnoses the lifetime mismatch; the symptom is an unrelated-looking crash from garbage data: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'" / "  what():  cannot store a negative time point in rclcpp::Time" (https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/469). The use-after-free was found only with Valgrind ("Invalid read of size 8" ... "Address 0x61084f0 is 0 bytes inside a block of size 8 free'd"), and a team member notes "the application may happily run reading forbidden memory without any error".

resolution.summary: Humble: rcl makes disable_loaned_message true by default (loans only if ROS_DISABLE_LOANED_MESSAGES=0; rcl#1116, backport of rcl#1110, in rcl 5.3.6), so rclcpp no longer takes loaned messages; rclcpp adds a one-time warning when loans are still enabled ("Loaned messages are only safe with const ref subscription callbacks."; rclcpp#2364, backport of #2335, in 16.0.7). Alternative confirmed by the reporter: rclcpp#2092 (rolling only), which makes ClocksState::cache_last_msg store a copy instead of the loaned pointer.
resolution.evidence: Maintainer closing note: "We disabled loans by default via https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/pull/2335 and https://github.com/ros2/rcl/pull/1110" / "We backported the above to Humble and Iron." / "The above works around the issue." (https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/469#issuecomment-1877574593). No source shows the Humble fix running in this composition. For rclcpp#2092 the reporter answers "Yes, it does fix the issue for us." (https://github.com/ros2/rmw_cyclonedds/issues/469#issuecomment-1723688992) without naming the revisions tested, and the initial report says "It doesn't happen in ros:iron and ros:rolling" (different revisions of both units).

notes: Eligibility is a judgement call: all of the faulty logic is in rclcpp (a maintainer calls it "probably a bug in rclcpp"), and it would hit any loan-capable RMW (the rclcpp#2335 description cites the same effect with Fast-DDS from Nav2); I treat it as an interface failure because it is rclcpp returning a loan across the RMW API while still using the loaned memory, and it only occurs when the peer loans. The failed-condition class is `other` (ownership/lifetime of loaned memory; no specific class exists). The resolution's decisive change is in rcl (a third unit between rclcpp and the RMW: 5.3.4 -> 5.3.6, commit 2c83ad3a), not in either specified unit; rclcpp 16.0.7's own change only warns. Other compositions/defects addressed by the same fixes and not conditions of this case: rclcpp's MessagePoolMemoryStrategy reusing messages still referenced by user shared_ptrs (demonstrated by the reporter with a standalone publisher/subscriber; fixed in rclcpp#2336), and the loaned-message path ignoring a custom memory strategy (mentioned in rclcpp#2335). Iceoryx (RouDi) and Cyclone DDS provide the shared-memory chunk underneath rmw_cyclonedds_cpp; the /clock publisher (`ros2 topic pub`) only supplies traffic. Of the packet's fix_refs, rclcpp#864 is the 2019 "Zero copy api" PR that introduced the loan path (origin, not a fix) and ros2_documentation#5068 (2025) is documentation of loaned messages. Re-enabling loans with shared_ptr callbacks is tracked in rclcpp#2401. The field element uses the C struct form field:rmw/rmw_subscription_t.can_loan_messages (package rmw, struct rmw_subscription_t). detection_stage is `activate` because the crash occurs during node startup (NodeTimeSource construction reading the cached clock message).
